subject: Automation request — Art. 28 evidence and DPIA operational matrix
messages:
From: Margaret Chen <margaret.chen@finserv.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.example.com>
Cc: privacyops@finserv.com
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence automation request — Art. 28 & DPIA operational matrix

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call today. To keep our procurement timeline on track we need a compact, machine-readable bundle that covers:

- Art. 28 processor appendix (manifest of subprocessors and transfer safeguards)
- Article 30 processing activities ledger excerpt for our EU processing scope
- DPIA support summary that maps your controls to our high-risk data flows
- An audit-runbook (steps + point contacts) for scheduled and ad-hoc evidence requests

Two asks to make this actionable for us:
1) Can Redwood provide an automated export (CSV/JSON) of the subprocessor inventory and last-updated timestamps?
2) Do you have a templated runbook we can integrate into our audit tooling (we use Confluence + an S3 evidence bucket)?

We're targeting signature and evidence readiness by 2027-08-12. If you can attach a sample runbook and the subprocessor extract that would be very helpful.

Best,
Margaret Chen
Senior Privacy Manager — FinServ Bank
privacyops@finserv.com

[Attachment: request_summary_finserv.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.example.com>
To: Margaret Chen <margaret.chen@finserv.com>
Cc: privacyops@finserv.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence automation request — Art. 28 & DPIA operational matrix

Hi Margaret — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (Privacy Ops) and Karthik (Product) to capture the export requirements and the runbook artifact.

Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can export a machine-readable subprocessor inventory with timestamps (CSV + JSON).
- We have an internal "DPIA runbook" that we can adapt to include customer-facing escalation steps, evidence bucket paths, and an audit checklist.

Questions for you:
- Which fields do you need in the subprocessor extract beyond name, country, purpose, legal basis, and last-reviewed? (e.g., SOC/Security attestations, contact, contract date?)
- For the DPIA mapping, is a two-page summary OK or do you want the full control-matrix (we can provide both; summary + linked artifact)?

I'll attach the initial runbook draft and a redacted sample of the subprocessor CSV so you can confirm the schema. Karthik — can you confirm whether the export will include transfer mechanism tags (SCCs, adequacy, standard contractual clauses) and a last-transfer-check timestamp?

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior GTM Privacy Liaison | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: dpiarunbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 780KB)]
[Attachment: art28_inventory.csv (CSV, 18KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Margaret Chen <margaret.chen@finserv.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.example.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 10:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence automation request — Art. 28 & DPIA operational matrix

Margaret / Camila — quick technical note on the export and runbook integration: 

1) Subprocessor export:
- We'll provide CSV and JSON exports. Fields included: subprocessor_id, name, role, country, legal_basis (SCC/adequacy/other), attestations (SOC2/ISO27001), contract_signed_at, last_reviewed_at, contact_email, data_categories_processed, transfer_mechanism_tag.
- Exports are generated from our compliance service and timestamped. We'll include a checksum and a "generated_at" ISO field for replayability.

2) DPIA runbook:
- We maintain a two-layer artifact: an executive 2-page summary (controls mapped to your high-risk flows) and an operational playbook (step-by-step evidence collection, S3 path conventions, retention metadata, audit owner contacts).
- For automated evidence delivery we support S3 pushes (presigned URLs) and a limited-time share to customer buckets. We can also create a Confluence-friendly markdown export.

3) Proposed integration flow (short):
- Redwood compliance service pushes a daily subprocessor export to s3://redwood-evidence/finserv/ (or to your bucket if you prefer).
- On-demand requests are handled via a signed URL valid for 7 days; ad-hoc audits trigger a webhook to your privacyops email.

Action items:
- Margaret: confirm fields you want in the CSV/JSON (I listed our standard set).
- Camila/Laura: I'll prepare a sample generated export and a Confluence markdown of the runbook.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Product Manager, Compliance Integrations | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: sample_export_art28.json (JSON, 6KB)]

From: Margaret Chen <margaret.chen@finserv.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: privacyops@finserv.com
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence automation request — Art. 28 & DPIA operational matrix

Camila / Karthik — this looks great, thank you.

We confirm the fields Karthik listed are sufficient; please include attestations and contact email in the export. The S3 push into s3://redwood-evidence/finserv/ works for us — we'll configure our ingestion to pull daily.

For the runbook: we prefer the two-page executive summary plus the operational markdown. If you can include the webhook format for ad-hoc audits (payload example) that's perfect.

Next steps:
- Karthik: send sample export + webhook payload example by 2027-08-04.
- Camila: include runbook + Confluence markdown and a short statement of who will be our audit contact (name + email) by 2027-08-05.

I'll loop Procurement once we have the artifacts for final sign-off.

Regards,
Margaret Chen
Senior Privacy Manager — FinServ Bank
